messages.content: Write the introduction to a guide for a REST API that manages calendar bookings. Around 200 words.

The Calendar Bookings API lets you manage time-based reservations programmatically. Automate scheduling across your platform.

Build scheduling platforms, add booking capabilities to existing applications, or streamline appointment workflows. This API provides endpoints to create, retrieve, update, and cancel bookings—everything you need to run a booking system.

The API uses REST conventions and JSON for all payloads. Communication happens over HTTPS with API key authentication in request headers. Key capabilities include creating bookings with customizable time slots and metadata, querying available time windows to prevent double-bookings, modifying existing reservations, and canceling bookings with optional notification triggers. The API also supports pagination for listing operations, webhooks for real-time updates when bookings change, and consistent status codes and error messages for reliable edge-case handling.

Before you start, get an API key from your dashboard. Every endpoint requires authentication, and requests are rate-limited to prevent abuse.

This guide walks through authentication, endpoints, request and response formats, and error handling strategies. We've included code examples in popular languages and provided access to a sandbox environment for testing before production deployment.

The API uses REST conventions and JSON for all payloads. Communication happens over HTTPS with API key authentication in request headers. Key capabilities include creating bookings with customizable time slots and metadata, querying available time windows to prevent double-bookings, modifying existing reservations, and canceling bookings with optional notification triggers. The API also supports pagination for listing operations, webhooks for real-time updates when bookings change, and consistent status codes and error messages for reliable edge-case handling.

All requests to the Calendar Bookings API require an API key passed as the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. Generate and manage API keys from your account dashboard, where you can create multiple keys for different applications or environments. Treat API keys as secrets—never commit them to version control or expose them in client-side code. For server-to-server communication, pass the key directly in request headers. If you're building a client-side application, store the key securely on your backend and proxy requests through your server. Each API key is associated with specific permissions and rate limits tied to your account plan.

Rewrite it for someone who has never used a REST API before.

The Calendar Bookings API lets you manage time-based reservations programmatically. Think of it as a way to automate scheduling—instead of manually managing bookings, you can let software handle it for you.

An API is like a communication channel between your application and our booking system. You send a request (like "create a booking for tomorrow at 2pm"), and the system sends back a response (like "booking confirmed"). REST just means we follow a standard format for these conversations—no special knowledge required to understand how it works.

You can create bookings with custom time slots, check which times are available to avoid double-bookings, change existing reservations, and cancel bookings. The system can automatically notify people when their booking changes, and it organizes results into pages so you're not overwhelmed by too much data at once.

Every request needs an API key—a password-like token that proves you're allowed to access your bookings. Add it to your request, and the system trusts that it's you. Get your key from your account dashboard. Keep it as a secret that you don't share, don't put in websites, and don't expose in your code. If you're building a website, store the key safely on your server and have your server make the requests instead of doing it directly from someone's browser.

This guide explains everything step-by-step, with examples in common programming languages and a safe testing environment to practice before going live.

The Calendar Bookings API lets you manage time-based reservations programmatically. Think of it as a way to automate scheduling—instead of manually managing bookings, you can let software handle it for you.

An API is like a communication channel between your application and our booking system. You send a request (like "create a booking for tomorrow at 2pm"), and the system sends back a response (like "booking confirmed"). REST just means we follow a standard format for these conversations—no special knowledge required to understand how it works.

You can create bookings with custom time slots, check which times are available to avoid double-bookings, change existing reservations, and cancel bookings. The system can automatically notify people when their booking changes, and it organizes results into pages so you're not overwhelmed by too much data at once.

Every request needs an API key—a password-like token that proves you're allowed to access your bookings. Add it to your request, and the system trusts that it's you. Get your key from your account dashboard. Keep it as a secret that you don't share, don't put in websites, and don't expose in your code. If you're building a website, store the key safely on your server and have your server make the requests instead of doing it directly from someone's browser.

The API enforces rate limits to keep the service stable for everyone. Your plan includes a maximum number of requests per minute—if you exceed this, the API will temporarily reject requests with a "too many requests" error. Design your application to space out requests or batch operations when possible. If you consistently hit rate limits, you can upgrade your plan for higher allowances.

This guide explains everything step-by-step, with examples in common programming languages and a safe testing environment to practice before going live.
